study.name: Multivariate patterns of food image evaluations distinguish obesity: A key role of highly processed foods
study.citation: Toyama, A., Yamashita, Y., & Suzuki, S. (2026). Multivariate patterns of food image evaluations distinguish obesity: A key role of highly processed foods. Appetite, 227, 108712. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.appet.2026.108712

description: Likability ratings for all 896 images of the food-pics_extended database, collected online in Japan (CrowdWorks) between January and March 2025. Participants answered "Do you like the food?" on an eight-point Likert scale (1 = strongly disagree, 8 = strongly agree). Each of three days covered one dimension -- likability, tastiness or healthiness -- with task order counterbalanced; only the likability ratings are held here. IMPORTANT: the sample is stratified by body mass index, not drawn from the general population. Participants were recruited into an obese group (BMI >= 30) and a lean group (BMI < 25), and the 200 analysed here are 107 lean and 93 obese. Treat marginal means accordingly. Item names come from the food-pics description of each image; the set gives several distinct images the same description, so the 896 images collapse to 592 named items and a subject's ratings of same-named images are averaged, as in toyam. This is a different sample from toyam, which the paper describes as its pilot study: no subject's ratings match between the two.
